newsitem.title: INDIA: India winter groundnut output seen up at 6.2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: India winter groundnut output seen up at 6.2 mln T.

text.p: India's winter groundnut output is expected to be around 6.2 million tonnes, up from last year's 4.85 million, industry officials said on Friday.
"The increase in output would be due to good rainfall in Gujarat," said G.K. Sood, executive director of the Vanaspati Manufacturers Association of India.
India produces two groundnut crops in a year. The winter crop is sown during June-July and harvested in October.
Saurashtra, in the western state of Gujarat, produces about one-third of the country's annual groundnut output of 7.0 million tonnes.

Sood said Gujarat's winter groundnut output in 1995/96 (November-October) was only one million tonnes as scanty monsoon rains had affected production. This year it was expected to be around 2-2.2 million tonnes, he said.
"In Saurashtra, the crop is excellently progressing," said Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.
"But widespread rains are required in the month of September for the final growth. Otherwise output could fall by 40 percent," he said.
"If we get enough rainfall in the next few weeks an output of nearly 1.8 million tonnes from Saurashtra region can be expected," said one analyst.
"Otherwise the output might fall to 1.2 million tonnes."
The analyst said the crop would be slightly delayed as some of the groundnut-growing regions had received late rains.
India's southwest monsoon hit the southern state of Kerala in the first week of June. But rains did not hit some western pockets till mid-July, delaying sowing operations.
The southern states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh are the other major groundnut producers.
The analyst said the three southern Indian states would account for nearly three million tonnes of groundnut in the current season compared to 2.5 million tonnes in the previous season.
"The crop in the southern states are also progressing well," he said.
The states of Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa account for India's remaining groundnut output.
